steps.title: Create project folder
steps.instruction: Create a main project folder named HD_digital_biomarker_analysis for the digital biomarker analysis.

steps.title: Install Python
steps.instruction: Install Python version 3.8 or later on the analysis workstation.

steps.title: Install required packages
steps.instruction: Install all required Python packages for data processing, statistics, machine learning, and visualization.

steps.title: Place analysis scripts
steps.instruction: Copy all Python analysis scripts into the scripts/ subfolder of the project folder.

steps.title: Add video recordings
steps.instruction: Place all participant video files into the raw_video/ folder within the project directory.

steps.title: Extract facial features
steps.instruction: Run the facial feature extraction script on the videos.

steps.title: Check facial feature quality
steps.instruction: Inspect the extracted facial feature table for ID correctness, missing values, and extreme outliers.

substeps.instruction: Confirm that participant IDs are correctly extracted.
Check missing values for each facial feature.
Identify extreme outliers that may result from failed landmark detection.

steps.title: Add audio recordings
steps.instruction: Place all participant audio files into the raw_audio/ folder, naming each file with the participant ID (e.g., sub001_audio.wav) and using a consistent .wav format when possible.

substeps.instruction: Ensure each audio file is named using the participant ID.
Use a consistent audio format; recommended .wav.

steps.title: Extract speech features
steps.instruction: Open a terminal, cd into HD_digital_biomarker_analysis, and run the speech feature extraction script.

substeps.instruction: Open the terminal and enter the project folder: cd HD_digital_biomarker_analysis
Save the extracted speech features into intermediate_results/ as speech_features.csv.

steps.title: Check speech feature quality
steps.instruction: Inspect the extracted speech feature table for ID correctness, number of processed files, and missing values.

substeps.instruction: Confirm that participant IDs are correctly extracted.
Check the number of successfully processed audio files.
Check missing values for each speech feature.

steps.title: Place integrated feature table
steps.instruction: Place the integrated spreadsheet containing facial and speech features into the project folder.

steps.title: Merge all data tables
steps.instruction: Merge facial feature table, speech feature table, and clinical information table by participant ID, ensuring consistent diagnostic group labels, and complete age and sex for all participants.

substeps.instruction: Use participant ID as the key variable.
Confirm that diagnostic group labels are consistent (e.g., HD, HC).
Confirm that age and sex are complete for all included participants.

steps.title: Define feature categories
steps.instruction: Classify features into facial and speech domains and save the list for reproducibility.

substeps.instruction: Facial features may include facial movement variability, regional facial movement metrics, and blink-related features.
Speech features may include fundamental frequency, loudness regulation, phonation instability, and temporal features.
Save the feature list as feature_category_list.xlsx.

steps.title: Run group comparison
steps.instruction: Execute the statistical comparison script to compare each facial and speech feature between HD and HC groups, using age and sex as covariates where appropriate (model: Feature ~ Group + Age + Sex).

substeps.instruction: Open terminal, cd into project folder.
Compare each facial and speech feature between the HD and HC groups.
Use age and sex as covariates when appropriate; recommended model Feature ~ Group + Age + Sex.

steps.title: Correct for multiple testing
steps.instruction: Apply false discovery rate (FDR) correction to all feature‑level raw p values and report both raw and FDR‑adjusted p values.

substeps.instruction: Collect raw p values from all tested facial and speech features.
Report both raw p values and FDR‑adjusted p values.

steps.title: Generate comparison plots
steps.instruction: Create visualizations (boxplots, violin plots, or dot plots) to display group differences for disease‑associated features.

substeps.instruction: Use boxplots, violin plots, or dot plots to show group differences.

steps.title: Run ROC analysis
steps.instruction: Execute the ROC analysis script to calculate ROC curves and AUC for each individual facial and speech feature.

substeps.instruction: Open terminal, cd into project folder.
Calculate ROC curves for individual facial and speech features.
Calculate the area under the curve for each feature.

steps.title: Summarize ROC performance
steps.instruction: For each feature, report AUC, sensitivity, specificity, optimal cutoff (if applicable) and save the table as ROC_results.xlsx.

substeps.instruction: For each feature, report AUC, sensitivity, specificity, optimal cutoff if applicable.
Save the ROC result table as ROC_results.xlsx.

steps.title: Prepare machine‑learning dataset
steps.instruction: Construct the feature matrix including participants with complete group label, age, sex, and behavioral feature data; define outcome variable (HD=1, HC=0) and predictors (facial, speech, age, sex).

substeps.instruction: Include participants with complete group label, age, sex, and behavioral feature data.
Define the outcome variable as diagnostic group (HD=1, HC=0).
Define predictors as facial features, speech features, age, and sex.

steps.title: Split dataset into train/test
steps.instruction: Perform a stratified 70:30 split, assigning 70% of participants to the training set and 30% to an independent test set, which must be held out throughout model development and not used for screening, preprocessing, cross‑validation, or model selection.

substeps.instruction: Use a stratified 70:30 train‑test split.
Assign 70% of participants to the training set.
Assign 30% of participants to the independent test set.
Hold out the test set throughout model development.
Do not use the test set for feature screening, preprocessing, cross‑validation, or model selection.

steps.title: Create stratified cross‑validation folds
steps.instruction: Within the training set, generate five stratified folds; for each iteration, use four folds for model training and the remaining fold for validation, rotating until each fold has served as validation once.

substeps.instruction: Split the training set into five stratified folds.
For each fold, use four folds for model training.
Repeat until each fold has been used once as the validation fold.

steps.title: Feature screening in training folds
steps.instruction: Within each training‑fold subset, perform univariate logistic regression to screen behavioral features, keeping age and sex as fixed covariates, and never using the independent test set for screening.

substeps.instruction: Use univariate logistic regression to screen behavioral features.
Do not use the independent test set for feature screening.
Keep age and sex as fixed covariates regardless of screening results.

steps.title: Standardize features in pipeline
steps.instruction: Fit a scaler on each fold‑specific training subset, apply it to the corresponding validation fold, and for final test‑set evaluation fit the scaler on the full training set and apply to the independent test set.

substeps.instruction: Fit the scaler on the fold‑specific training subset.
Apply the fitted scaler to the corresponding validation fold.
For final test‑set evaluation, fit the scaler on the full training set only.
Apply the fitted scaler to the independent test set.

steps.title: Train classification models
steps.instruction: Train machine‑learning classifiers using the training data.

steps.title: Evaluate final model on test set
steps.instruction: Retrain the selected model on the full training set, fit only on training data, apply it to the held‑out test set, and save predictions as test_set_predictions.csv.

substeps.instruction: Use only the training set for final model fitting.
Apply the final model to the held‑out test set.
Save the test‑set prediction results as test_set_predictions.csv.

steps.title: Run machine‑learning script
steps.instruction: Open a terminal, cd into the project folder, and execute the machine‑learning script; then save the model performance table as machine_learning_performance.xlsx.

substeps.instruction: Open the terminal and enter the project folder: cd HD_digital_biomarker_analysis
Save the model performance table as machine_learning_performance.xlsx.

steps.title: Prepare clinical outcome variables
steps.instruction: Gather clinical scales for association analysis and check for missing values in each scale.

substeps.instruction: Check missing values for each clinical scale.

steps.title: Test biomarker‑clinical associations
steps.instruction: Assess associations between digital biomarkers and clinical outcomes using regression models adjusted for age and sex (model: Clinical outcome ~ Digital biomarker + Age + Sex) and apply FDR correction across all tests.

substeps.instruction: Use regression models when adjusting for age and sex; recommended model Clinical outcome ~ Digital biomarker + Age + Sex.
Apply FDR correction across multiple feature‑clinical association tests.

steps.title: Organize final outputs
steps.instruction: Collect all final result files into a single location.
